title: Decision: no OAuth or OIDC at the agent's boundary; social login belongs at the provider and arrives as an app password
description:
DECIDED (Mark 2026-11-24). No OAuth and no OIDC at the agent's boundary. Social
login is a provider matter (epic mimid-hb5z), and what reaches the agent is an
ordinary named app password.

WHY. "Create account with Google" at the agent is close to meaningless:

- The agent serves exactly one user and has no account to create. It is already
  theirs, keyed to their MIMI URI.
- The first credential has to exist before any browser flow could run, so the
  flow cannot be how a user gets in.
- It would make logging in to a daemon on your own laptop depend on an internet
  round trip to Google, and hand Google a lockout lever over your own chat
  history.
- The agent holds MLS keys and plaintext. An IdP-authenticated session may mint
  a credential; it must never be able to extract key material.
- Linking Google must not make Google an authority over an MLS identity.
  Credential type (BasicCredential today, did:webvh, X.509) is a separate
  question from how a user logs in.

So docs/design/frontend-auth.md §4.2's "No OAuth" for JMAP and §4.1's "Not
offered: ... OAUTHBEARER" for IRC are confirmed, and this bead is why, not just
that.

WHAT SOCIAL LOGIN LOOKS LIKE INSTEAD, at the agent: token exchange, which is
what mimid already does. The user authenticates with Google at the PROVIDER in a
browser; the result of that session is a named app password; the client then uses
it with SASL PLAIN, SASL SCRAM-SHA-256, HTTP Basic or Bearer. This is the
Fastmail IMAP app-password pattern, and `mimid-agent <config> setup <client>
<device>` with its QR code is already the delivery mechanism. Social login
becomes one more route into credential minting rather than a new mechanism at
the boundary. Beads mimid-e13m.15 and mimid-e13m.16.

ON SASL OAUTHBEARER (RFC 7628). It is the correct IRC mechanism and IRCv3 SASL
carries it fine. The blocker is client support: Goguma, HexChat and WeeChat do
not implement it (*from memory, verify before relying on this*). Offering only
OAUTHBEARER would mean no stock IRC client could log in, which is the opposite
of what epic mimid-e13m is for.
